openPoints: RESOLVED — TIER 3 (the projection wrote `suspended` and announced nothing). Verified on disk against the claim, both halves. No double-emission: recall-projection.ts:105 skips a cell whose authority row already reads `suspended`, so the second projection of a batch returns an empty set; on the final batch RecallWorker.processBatch (recall-worker.ts:111 then :134) calls checkpoint AND complete with the same case, and the second call announces nothing. The worker's own `this.emit` at recall-worker.ts:124 is a bounded in-memory debug ring (:47-52), not the session bus, so it is not a second channel. No missed cell: both eap-repositories.ts checkpoint and complete return the projection's `suspendedCells` out of the serialTransaction and call announce() after it returns, and interruptAndResume drives the same two methods. The old last-batch-only loop at eap.ts:919 is gone. Emission is per cell at the moment of projection, commit-then-broadcast, and the kind is in ALWAYS_BROADCAST_KINDS (state.ts:241). No further deduction.

RESOLVED — TIER 3 cluster (advertised contract, unknown candidate state, dead `checkpoint`, silent exhaustion). transport.ts now advertises `evidence` (required, minItems 1), `candidateIds` (required, minItems 1), `basedOnSeq` (bounded to MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) and `batchSize` on the tools that validate them, and the command enum matches nextStateMap. eap.ts:265 checks CANDIDATE_STATES at runtime and refuses ILLEGAL_TRANSITION instead of falling back to `deliberated`, and the `?? { command: 'DELIBERATE' }` fallback is deleted. `checkpoint` is refused MALFORMED_CONTRACT (eap.ts:798) rather than validated and discarded. recallOutcome (eap.ts:955-966) always carries `complete` and `remainingClaimIds`, both backed by real domain fields (recall.ts:37,231). eapPropose is now wrapped in storedStateRefusal like eapPromote. `-0` is excluded from basedOnSeq. No further deduction.

TIER 2 — Whole-tenant materialization, carried forward, disclosed and deducted once as a cluster. Unchanged: structuredClone of state.graphs and state.claimsCache per admission, the roundtrip-index spread per candidate in incrementalGate, and buildRecallExecutionContext (dependency-query.ts:77,89,95) loading every claim, every candidate and every authority row of the tenant into three Maps. One correction to my last verdict in the implementer's favour: recallContext() is called once per command at eap.ts:893, outside the drive loop, not once per batch — so this is linear in tenant size per recall, not quadratic. It is still the whole tenant in memory on a hot path with no bound and no streaming. For a 100k-claim tenant, what is the event loop doing for the duration of an admission burst, and what is the resident set of one recall command?

TIER 3 — NEW, and introduced by this commit rather than inherited. findRecallClosureMembership (recall-closure.ts) selects EVERY recall_cases row of the tenant, ORDER BY created_at, id — and db.ts declares no index on recall_cases at all, so that is a table scan plus a filesort — then JSON.parse's each `closure` blob until it finds the claim. It is called once per VERIFY (eap.ts:314) and, worse, once per candidate inside the promotion loop (eap.ts:493), so promoting 50 candidates re-scans and re-parses the tenant's entire recall history 50 times, inside the promote unit of work. Every other tenant-scoped table in db.ts got an index (idx_candidates_tenant_horizon, idx_contestations_tenant_seq, idx_promotion_events_ordinal). Why is the one new gate that runs on every lifecycle completion the one that reads an unindexed table and parses a JSON blob per row, and what does a tenant with a thousand recall cases pay per promote?

TIER 3 — NEW, and the far side of the gate you correctly added. recall-closure.ts matches on membership in ANY closure with no status predicate, so once a recall case exists, every claim in its reverse closure is permanently refused VERIFY and promotion. That is right for the direct targets. For an indirect dependent it is a one-way door: the refusal text says it 'cannot complete its lifecycle without new proof', but no tool on the surface accepts that proof or clears closure membership, and 003 defers the destination status, so nothing will ever move the claim. The stalled-recall variant is sharper: `batchLimitReached` returns an `obligation` instructing the operator to 'Re-drive the case with a larger batchSize', while the replay branch at eap.ts:863 returns unconditionally for any existing case — so the only tool that could re-drive it replays it instead, and the retry drops `batchLimitReached`, `maxBatches` and the obligation text entirely (eap.ts:886 hardcodes false), leaving `complete:false` with no reason and no remedy. If the closure is frozen and the documented remedy is unreachable through the MCP surface, what does the operator do that is not a manual SQL edit?

TIER 3 — Carried forward, disclosed and unfixed, deducted once as a cluster: eapInitiate is still the one adapter outside serialTransaction while HorizonStore.create does read-then-upsert; persistent-delta still takes COALESCE(MAX(seq),0) for cs_deltas inside a DEFERRED unit; getEvents, getProposalsForParent and the audit list() still materialize whole tenant tables with no pagination; promotion_events still has no retention policy while capability_executions has one; client/src/eap.ts still sends basedOnSeq ?? 0. Why does the capability audit get a bounded-growth policy and the promotion event log, which grows on the same traffic, not?

TIER 4 — Raised, NOT deducted (rule 7: a lone low-tier item does not move the score). The announcement is real but it left the unit of work that the codebase already has a mechanism for. changeset.ts:386 pairs an authority write with appendEvent(..., { defer: true }) INSIDE inTx, so the durable `events` row commits with the write and only the push to sessions waits for the commit. SqliteRecallRepository.announce runs the whole appendEvent after serialTransaction has returned, so the events row is written in its own implicit transaction: a failure between the two leaves `authority` at `suspended` with no row in the append-only log a reconnecting session replays from. The window is same-tick and narrow. Separately, nothing renders the kind — system-message.ts:60 has a case for authority.flipped and none for this, and no client handler exists — so 003's 'authority view' consumer is still notional. Why was `{ defer: true }` not the mechanism here?
architectureTip: The gate is correct to fail closed on a decision the spec defers, but a refusal that names a remedy the surface cannot perform is a dead end rather than a gate: pair every terminal refusal with a modelled transition that can clear it — a rehabilitation command that supplies new proof, and an operator-driven resume that re-enters an unfinished case instead of replaying it — so that no durable state is reachable from which the tool surface offers no exit.
